 Awar D
1.

By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 filed by the petitioner Salimuddin with respect to the injures caused to him in a vehicular on 28.10.2020 2.

The facts of the case are that on that day, the petitioner Salimuddin along with his brothers Abdul Salam and Fahimuddin and friends Zahid & Salman, were going to their home Rabupura after attending a marriage ceremony in Bulandshahar by their car bearing no MH-14-DA-0209.
When the they reached near village Sikheda, a truck bearing registration no. RJ-14GG-8661 (offending vehicle) was coming from Bulandshahar.
The driver of the truck was driving it in a rash and negligent manner.
The truck hit their car and two other vehicles and caused the accident.
The driver of the truck was Raham Deen.
He is also the owner of the truck.
In that accident, Zahid and Salman died on the spot and the petitioner and his brother were injured.
The petitioner was taken to Babu Banarasi Das Hospital Meerut, where he was referred to Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel Hospital.
Petitioner was also later on treated in Raj Hospital, Rabupura G.B. Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.
According to the petition, the petitioner remained bed ridden for about four months and that the petitioner suffered multiple injuries, chest pain and his body pain.

3. The respondent no.1 Raham Deen who is the driver and owner of the offending truck has taken the defence that the accident happened due to the fault of a third vehicle, a tempo which tried to overtake his truck due to which he had to apply sudden breaks to save that vehicle.
The respondent no. 2 insurance company has taken the general defences.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 02.06.2022 (i) Whether the Petitioner Salimuddin Khan suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 28.10.2020at 5.00 p.m., near Village Sikheda, Bulanshahar, U.P. within jurisdiction of PS Kotwali Dehat, due to rash and negligent driving of trailer (Tata motor 18 tyres) bearing registration No.RJ14GG8661 being driven by respondent No.1 /Raham Deen?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

(OPP) 
5.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Salimuddin Khan has examined himself as PW-1 but the respondents did not lead any evidence.
6. I have heard Mr. Fakhruddin, counsel for petitioner, and Mr. Naved Rajpur counsel for respondent no. 1 and Ms. Sonali Aggarwal counsel for no. 2/insurer and perused the records.

2 7.

The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE NO.1: (i) Whether the Petitioner Salimuddin Khan suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 28.10.2020at 5.00 p.m., near Village Sikheda, Bulanshahar, U.P.
within jurisdiction of PS Kotwali Dehat, due to rash and negligent driving of trailer (Tata motor 18 tyres) bearing registration No.RJ- 14GG8661 being driven by respondent No.1 /Rahamdeen? (OPP)
8.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
9. Now in this case, the petitioner is the injured and witness of the accident.

In order to establish his claim, petitioner Salimuddin has examined himself as PW-1 and proved his Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/1,
copy of Bank passbook Ex.PW1/2, copy of chargesheet Ex.PW1/3, medical treatment documents Ex.PW1/4 (Colly), MLC Ex.PW1/5, PAN card Ex.PW1/6.
He also stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the truck.

He has deposed that on the fateful day i.e. he along with his brothers namely Abdul Salam and &
Fahimuddin and friends Zahid & Salman were going to their home Rabupura after attending a marriage ceremony in Bulandshahar U.P by car registration no MH-14- DA-0209 and when they reached near village Sikheda, the offending vehicle registration no. RJ-14GG-8661, trailer (Tata Motors 18 tyres) was coming from Bulandshahar.
It was being driven rashly and negligently at excessive speed and dashed in the petitioner's car and other two vehicles with the forceful impact from behind.
As a result the car fall in ditch and the offending vehicle also fall over his car.
Driver Zahid And Salman died on the spot.
He and his brothers sustained grievous injuries.
He suffered multiple injuries on his body.
Due to the forceful impact by the offending vehicle, the car of the petitioner was also damaged.

10. Last but not the least, the respondent no. 1 has not denied the accident or the involvement of his vehicle but has only said that the accident occurred due to the fault of a third vehicle - a tempo.
Although he has averred about this defence in his reply but has not proved anything in this regard.
Further, none of the respondents have led any evidence to prove anything contrary to claim of petitioner.
11. In view of above, it is proved that petitioner sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1, the driver of the offending truck.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE NO. 2: Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
Salimuddin vs . Raham Deen & Ors.

3 12.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

13. In the case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, the Hon'ble Supreme Court while delineating on the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases observed that the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 ("the Act"), for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under head (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injuries, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the head (ii) (b), (iii), (v)
Salimuddin vs . Raham Deen & Ors.

on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76199037/
4 and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
Assessment of pecuniary damages under item (i) and (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of the actuals and are easily ascertainable from evidence.
Award under the head of future medical expenses - item (iii) depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for future treatment and cost thereof.

Assessment of non-pecuniary damages - item (iv), (v) and (vi)
involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury, deprivation, disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.
Therefore, the compensation in this case is calculated as follows.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
14.
Petitioner has stated in his evidence affidavit that he has spent around Rs.1,00,000/- on his medical treatment.
However, his counsel has admitted that the bills proved on record are of Rs.53,600/-.
Therefore, I award Rs.53,600/- as medical expenses to the petitioner.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
15.
From the affidavit of the petitioner, there is no clarity that what kind of injuries were suffered by him.
Nor there is any cogent record of his hospitalisation.
In these circumstances, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.15,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
16. Petitioner has claimed that he remained in hospital for around four months but he has not placed on record anything to substantiate it.
In that event, it will not be possible to award any compensation under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 17.

The petitioner has claimed Rs.40,000/- for his conveyance and Rs.1,00,000/- for special diet but he has not proved the actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- each to petitioner as conveyance and special diet charges.
18. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
( DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Salimuddin vs . Raham Deen & Ors.

on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76199037/
5
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- as attendant charges.
19. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.15,000/- (5,000+5,000+5,000) under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES 20.
Further, the petitioner is granted Rs.5,000/- for loss of amenities.

21. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount

1 Medical Expenses Rs.53,600 /-
 2 Pain & Sufferings Rs.15,000 /-
 3 Conveyance & Special diet Rs.10,000/-

4 Attendant charges Rs.5,000/-
 5 Loss of amenities.

TOTAL Rs.88,600/-
Issue No. 3 (iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
Petitioner has pursued his case diligently.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 9% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

RELIEF:
23.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.88,600/- (Rs Eighty-Eight Thousand Six Hundred only) along with interest @
9% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.2, insurance company.

This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
24.
Form IV-B in terms of MCTAP are annexed herewith as Annexure A.
